title: Reopen returns an internal work order to Complete with its shop supplies
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed, whose Shop supplies amount is $15.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
  4. Click "Reopen Work Order".
  5. Click Reopen Work Order in the window.
  6. Open the Notes tab.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The document shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu offers "Reopen Work Order".

Step 4:

  • The window opens.

Step 5:

  • The status reads "Complete" with the "Internal" badge.
  • "Shop supplies" still reads $15.00.
  • The NO CHARGE document is gone from the Finance tab.
  • "Close Work Order" is offered again.
  • The page stays on the Finance tab.

Step 6:

  • A system note records the Reopen with the user and the time.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order)

  • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced). The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. The reversal credits and debits exactly the accounts the Close used.”
  • S2-R18: “Every classification change writes a read-only system note on the work order (Notes tab, author ShopView, with the user and the time) and an Audit Log row: Convert to No Charge ("Converted to No Charge by [user]. Category [name], original work order [number]. Prices, fees and discounts removed; costs and hours kept."), Change category (from, to, original work order kept or cleared), Convert to Billable ("Every line priced as a new line would be today. Category [name] removed."), Close (posting date, account), Reopen, and the line actions of Story 12 (S12-R6). Work order numbers in notes are links.”
  • S2-R13: “The classification is written on the work order when it is created, when its customer changes and when it is converted; the closed record carries it too, with the category. Lists, reports and integrations read it from there, never from the customer flag. Converting to no charge or to billable, changing the category, a shop supplies amount change, Make internal (S1-R11, on each work order), Close with its posting date, Reopen, and adding or removing a customer's Internal flag are recorded in the work order or customer Audit Log with the user and the time.”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026
